newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IAFF COUNCIL TO FOCUS ON ATHENS WORLD CHAMPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAFF COUNCIL TO FOCUS ON ATHENS WORLD CHAMPS.

text.p: A three-day council of the International Amateur Athletics Federation (IAAF) will focus on Athens' preparations to host the world championships in August and will discuss little else, officials said on Thursday.
"The main issue on the agenda is Athens' progress in view of the championship. I don't expect much else to be discussed," an IAAF official told Reuters.
The IAAF seemed to shun a petition from Canadian sprinter Ben Johnson to overturn a lifetime ban imposed in 1993 after twice testing positive for banned substances.

Johnson wants a Canadian court to rule that the ban was imposed unfairly and illegally and prevents him from earning a living. He hopes that a favourable ruling will influence his petition for reinstatement.
Johnson was stripped of his Olympic gold medal and world record in the 100 metres after testing positive for steroids in 1988.
"Johnson's case will probably come up in our next council in late July. In any case, it's not high on our agenda," the official said.
IAAF president Primo Nebiolo expressed confidence that Athens would successfully host the championships on August 1-10.
"We gave Athens our best event. I am sure it will do splendid," he told reporters upon arrival at Athens airport.

The championship is seen as a major test for Athens' bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games. Most members of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) will be in Athens in August before September's vote on the venue.

Athens lost the 1996 s Games to Atlanta because of its lack of organisation and poor infrastructure. It had threatened to boycott centennial Olympic festivities in Atlanta and never bid for the Games again.
But it has put together a much better bidding dossier for 2004 and is considered among the favourites along with Rome. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
